scope: Linux creator-thread parent-death lifecycle; public synthetic framed peer, no real secrets or funds

tests.name: TestKernelPdeathsigControlKillsChildWhenCreatorThreadRetires
tests.proof: Actual non-leader creator OS thread retires; direct Pdeathsig child is SIGKILLed while the Go test parent remains alive

tests.name: TestOwnedChildSurvivesCallerThreadRetirementAndReapsOnKill
tests.proof: Manifest-checked Child has a distinct live creator thread; original calling thread retires, a subsequent framed RPC succeeds, then Kill waits for owner release and child reaping

tests.name: TestRestartedChildrenReleaseEveryLifetimeOwner
tests.proof: Eight complete start/RPC/kill generations close every owner completion channel and reap every child

tests.name: TestOwnedChildDiesOnAbruptParentProcessDeath
tests.proof: Actual manifest-verified Child answers two private RPCs while parent lives; abrupt parent SIGKILL causes required child SIGKILL, independently reaped by an isolated subreaper. Peer waits on EOF, excluding pipe-close success.

implementation: Dedicated per-child goroutine locks its OS thread from cmd.Start through child kill and cmd.Wait; parent-death SIGKILL and Setpgid retained
limitations: These process/thread lifecycle regressions do not establish a clean OS/Wayland/suspend acceptance matrix
The isolated Linux mechanism is confirmed; the exact earlier packaged restart incident remains unproven without its thread/process trace
